summary: 1934 Kootenai NF lookout: main tower still listed as standing; its L-4 living-quarters cab collapsed in winter 2012-13. Current access unconfirmed.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower with 7x7 foot cab, plus a 10-foot pole tower with L-4 living-quarters cab
facts.status_note: The L-4 living-quarters cab on the 10-foot pole tower collapsed over winter 2012-2013; the Association's Montana list still shows the Warland Peak tower as standing.

events.note: Developed with a 100-foot steel tower and 7x7 foot cab, plus a 10-foot pole tower with L-4 living-quarters cab
Memoir author at Warland Ranger Station from spring 1939; names Rex Fleming as the lookout man. Year inferred from the memoir timeline.
Partial collapse: only the small L-4 living-quarters cab on the pole tower collapsed, over winter 2012-2013; no source reports the steel tower down
Registered January 9, 2021 as US 1506, MT 84; nominated by Kyle Stetler

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and the 2013 report give a 10-foot pole tower; the memoir describes CCC-built quarters on 12-foot tower legs. We keep 10 feet and flag the memoir's figure.
firelookout.com lists 5950 ft; NHLR lists 5,952 ft (1,814 m). The record's 1814.2 m matches NHLR.

sources.title: Early Days in the Forest Service (Volume 4)

notes_for_editor: Current access and rental status are not confirmed by any source read, so no access key is set. The 1939 date is inferred from the memoir timeline. Firelookout.com photo credits (Montana Memory Project, Gary Weber, Luke Channer) are not added because no image URLs or licences were checked. The brief's height_m 3.0 and design L-4 describe only the collapsed pole-tower quarters. Fact-check 2026-10-08: the FFLOS listing says only 'Tower Standing', so the story no longer says which tower; the 2013 event was relabelled from destroyed to other (partial collapse).
